learning_outcomes.text: Know the main properties of solid materials with semiconductor characteristics
Be able to use basic electronic devices (diodes, transistors, optoelectronic devices, and power devices) and understand their operation
Understand the operation of devices under biasing conditions
Know the operation of the operational amplifier and its applications
Be able to identify the main logic families and their characteristics
Be able to handle different types of logic gates in the laboratory and build digital circuits with them
Be able to analyze and design combinational and sequential circuits, understanding the basics of Digital Electronics
Acquire experience in laboratory work, using oscilloscopes, power supplies, signal generators, components, and assembly systems
Identify and use the fundamentals of electronics in general, explaining their applications
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics
Understand and interpret texts and data, developing skills for their concretization and clear and succinct presentation.
Be able to distribute resources and time and implement it in real situations.
Transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for seeking sustainable engineering solutions.
Actively collaborate with a group of people to achieve a common goal and develop multidisciplinary projects.
Establish relationships with other people with an open attitude.

Continuously use learning and develop autonomous and flexible learning strategies to facilitate professional insertion in diverse environments and with varied functions in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Gather and incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired and necessary training for the evolution of technique.
Develop own initiatives and undertake new projects, showing autonomy and creativity.

syllabus_topics: Semiconductor Materials - Conductors, insulators and semiconductors - Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors - Charge transport, carrier generation and recombination
Transistors - The bipolar transistor - The MOSFET transistor - Biasing and applications
Optoelectronic devices - Light-emitting diodes (LED) and photodetectors - Optocouplers
Power devices - Power diodes - Power transistors - Thyristors
The operational amplifier - Characteristics of the operational amplifier - Amplifier circuits - D/A and A/D converter circuits
Fundamentals of digital electronics - Boolean algebra and function simplification - Basic modules for logical function synthesis - Logic families
Combinational circuits - Analysis and synthesis of basic combinational circuits - Multiplexers and decoders
Sequential circuits - Bistable circuits - Analysis and synthesis of basic sequential circuits. Shift registers
Introduction to mechatronics - Measurement and control systems - Microcontrollers, sensors and actuators
Exercises and seminars related to theoretical content
Laboratory practices in Electronics - Diodes: I-V characteristics and rectification
Handling of logic gates and combinational circuits
Implementation of logical functions with multiplexers and decoders
Sequential circuits: flip-flops and shift registers

assessment_methods.method: Resolution of exercises and/or reports linked to laboratory practices

assessment_rules: The acquisition of competencies will be evaluated through continuous assessment activities and a final written test. If a score of 4 points or higher is obtained in the First Continuous Assessment Test, the Final Exam will have a weight of 35% and cover content not addressed in the first test; otherwise, it will weigh 70% and cover the entire syllabus. A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required in the Final Exam to be averaged with other activities; otherwise, the course cannot be passed. To pass the course, a minimum final score of 5 out of 10 is required, always meeting the minimum requirement in the Final Exam. In the extraordinary examination, a final written test will account for 70% of the grade, covering the entire syllabus, and practical work can be recovered with a specific test if a minimum of 5 points was not achieved.
